% A guard: it checks a case that the fix of the files read with the
% primitive \input must not break.
% LaTeX's dvipsnam.def, from TeX's tree, read with the primitive \input
% after xcolor. The file names itself \ProvidesFile{dvipsnam.def}, so
% tex4ht reads dvipsnam.4ht, which the TeX log lists. As in the PDF, a
% named color keeps its value.
% Two rules leave the name unmarked: it ends in .def, a package's
% extension, and it is found in TeX's tree and not beside the document.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xcolor}
\makeatletter
\input dvipsnam.def
\makeatother
\begin{document}
\textcolor[named]{BrickRed}{Brick red text.}
\end{document}
